resources.string: The keys show Aurebesh, the Star Wars alphabet. Your messages go out in normal letters: whoever gets them won\'t notice a thing.
Turn on Aurebesh in your phone settings
Choose Aurebesh as your current keyboard
To go back to the Samsung keyboard, hold the space bar.
Tap a field and type. If another keyboard shows up, you still need to choose Aurebesh.
Small Latin letter in the corner of each key, handy while you learn the alphabet
See what you type in Aurebesh
What you type and the suggestions are shown in Aurebesh above the keys. Your message is still sent in normal letters.
Adds a row above the keys with ✦ AI assistant, 😊 emoji, 📋 clipboard and one-handed mode, and ⚙ settings in ?123; without it the keyboard is shorter
Aurebesh has its own symbol for ch, sh, th, ae, eo, kh, ng and oo. On, you see them as that symbol. Off, letter by letter. Your message stays the same.
Row 1…0 above the letters; without it the keyboard is shorter and the numbers move to long-press on q⁠…⁠p
As you type you\'ll see up to three words above the keys. Tap one to use it. The highlighted one fixes typos and accents. Works without internet.
Accent menu: á à ä â…; slide and release
Punctuation menu: ? ! , : ; - \" \' @; release without moving for ?
Symbols laid out like Samsung Keyboard; 1/2 opens the second page with double letters, ¿ ¡ « » and more
Next Aurebesh language (shown when more than one is enabled)
Emoji panel by category, with recents; ABC returns to the letters
Everything you copied; tap to paste
Emoji you use will show up here
Plays a short audio file of yours (about 3 s or less) instead of the system click
Remembers the new words you use and which word you usually type after another, and suggests them. They are stored only on your phone.
Tap the space bar twice to end a sentence
Opens this settings screen from the keyboard
Copy some text and it will show up here. Tap an item to paste it.
Something may look different on your phone

This keyboard was tested on Samsung Galaxy phones with One UI 9. On yours (%1$s) some details may look different or misbehave. If that happens, hold the space bar to go back to your previous keyboard.
